items.title: Classification on the Basis of Substrates

source_refs.note: Classification on the Basis of Substrates: a main subheading of 5.7 Classification of enzymes, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 140-140.

blocks.text: Enzymes are also classified into following groups on the basis of their substrates.

items: Proteases: This group included the enzymes which catalyse the breakdown of proteins. For example, pepsin and trypsin enzymes catalyse the breakdown of large polypeptides into smaller polypeptides. Similarly, aminopeptidases further breakdown small polypeptides into dipeptides and erypsin breaks dipeptides into amino acids.
Lipases: These enzymes act upon lipids and catalyse their breakdown. For example, pancreatic lipase hydrolyses lipids into fatty acids and glycerol.

Carbohydrases: These enzymes act upon bigger carbohydrates and break them into smaller units. For example, amylase acts upon starch or glycogen and breaks them into maltose. Cellulase breaks cellulose into cellobiose (a disaccharide) or glucose. Similarly, maltase breaks down maltose into glucose, sucrase breaks sucrose into glucose and fructose, and lactase breaks lactose into glucose and galactose.
Nucleases: These enzymes act upon nucleic acids and catalyse their breakdown. For example, RNAase, DNAase, ATPase are responsible for the breakdown of RNA, DNA and ATP respectively.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The enzyme that breaks dipeptides into amino acids is erepsin; the book prints “erypsin”.

blocks.alt: A table with three columns, Class, Reaction type and Important subclasses, and six rows, each reaction drawn with lettered balls and reversible arrows. 1 Oxidoreductases: A (red) carrying two hydrogens + B (ox) to A (ox) + B (red); dehydrogenases, oxidases, reductases. 2 Transferases: A-B + C to A + C-B; phospho-, amino- and acyl-transferases. 3 Hydrolases: A-B + H2O to C + D; peptidases, lipases, glycosidases.
blocks.caption: Figure 5.12: Enzyme classification on the basis of reactions (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 5.12).
blocks.long_description: A table with three columns, Class, Reaction type and Important subclasses, and six rows, each reaction drawn with lettered balls and reversible arrows. 1 Oxidoreductases: A (red) carrying two hydrogens + B (ox) to A (ox) + B (red); dehydrogenases, oxidases, reductases. 2 Transferases: A-B + C to A + C-B; phospho-, amino- and acyl-transferases. 3 Hydrolases: A-B + H2O to C + D; peptidases, lipases, glycosidases. 4 Lyases: A carrying a small group to C + the group; decarboxylases, aldolases, synthases. 5 Isomerases: A to A with a part moved; epimerases, mutases, cis trans isomerases. 6 Ligases: A + B + ATP to A-B + ADP + phosphate; C-C, C-O, C-N ligases.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The printed Figure 5.12 names the third class 'Hydrases' and prints 'Glycodsidases'; the correct names are hydrolases and glycosidases, as drawn above.
